name: St. Methodius I, Patriarch of Constantinople
bio: J. M. Neale's headnote says S. Methodius I was a native of Syracuse who became a monk at Constantinople. Sent as legate from Pope Paschal to Michael the Stammerer, he was imprisoned for nine years for defending Icons, was scourged under the Emperor Theophilus, escaped, and when peace returned to the Church was raised to the throne of Constantinople. He assembled the synod that restored the Icons, which the Greeks celebrate on Orthodoxy Sunday, and died on 4 November 846. Neale's heading gives 836 instead.

Neale says his compositions are very few and are chiefly confined to Idiomela. This file gives Neale's 1862 version of the idiomela for a Sunday of the Fourth Tone, 'Are thy toils and woes increasing?'. He is a different man from Methodius of Olympus, the earlier martyr whose hymn Brownlie translated.

poems.title: Idiomela for a Sunday of the Fourth Tone
poems.author: St. Methodius I, Patriarch of Constantinople
poems.collection: Hymns of the Eastern Church (1862; 5th ed. 1884)
poems.text:
Are thy toils and woes increasing?
Are the Foe's attacks unceasing?
Look with Faith unclouded,
Gaze with eyes unshrouded,
On the Cross!

Dost thou fear that strictest trial?
Tremblest thou at Christ's denial?
Never rest without it,
Clasp thine hands about it,
—That dear Cross

Diabolic legions press thee?
Thoughts and works of sin distress thee?
It shall chase all terror,
It shall right all error,
That sweet Cross!

Draw’st thou nigh to Jordan's river?
Should’st thou tremble? Need’st thou quiver?
No! if by it lying,
No! if on it dying,
On the Cross!

Say then,—"Master, while I cherish
That sweet hope, I cannot perish!
After this life's story,
Give Thou me the glory
For the Cross!"
